=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh
  Line or code reference: 2196-2200 (inside the reviewer manifest loop), 2202-2204 (post-loop behavior)
  Problem: When multiple reviewer files have garbled checksums in a single editor attempt, each one emits its own ::warning::EDITOR_REVIEWER_CHECKSUM_UNVERIFIED attempt=<n> file=<path> expected_sha=<sha> path_entries=<n> checksum_matches=<n> line. A real typo (model garbled 1-2 hashes) is hard to distinguish from a fabricated entry (model claimed to read files it didn't), because both produce N warnings for N files. Operators scanning the workflow log have to manually count occurrences to distinguish the cases — the current implementation does not expose an aggregate count of checksum mismatches per attempt.
  Why it fails at runtime: After this PR, the checksum is warn-only and no longer a hard gate. The audit check (Review file issue audit:) still gates the attempt, but the audit is the same line the editor produces, so it doesn't independently verify the editor read the file. The per-file warning is the only signal that the editor's checksum claim is wrong; without an aggregate, a fabricated entry for one or two files slips by undetected by anyone not grepping + counting the warnings.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
